newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - NatWest straddle features in thin market.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - NatWest straddle features in thin market.

text.p: The UK traded options market was quiet at midday although institutional investors were getting back to their desks after a two-week break, dealers said.
A scarcity of corporate news and the weaker gilts market dampened enthusiasm for share derivatives, they said.
"Weaker gilts hasn't helped but until we get some corporate news, fund managers aren't going to take too many positions," one dealer said.
The FTSE 100 index was up 15.1 at 4,104.6 but the March gilt future eased 14/32 to 108-5/32 by 1225 GMT. A straddle buy in NatWest was the only significant trade of the morning.
The straddle was set up when one dealer bought 700 January 700 calls at 14p and at the same time bought 700 January 700 puts at 7p.
The straddle purchase allows the buyuer to make large potential profits if the underlying share moves far enough in either direction.
In this scenario, the buyer has a predetermined maximum loss, equal to the amount of the initial investment.
If Natwest shares are exactly at 700p at the time of expiration, the dealer will lose the initial investment of 21p plus commissions as both options would expire worthless.
NatWest shares were up 11-1/2p at 708p by 1225 GMT.
